title: fix: one signed-out sign-in pattern for enter dashboard
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Signed-out pages had two sign-in patterns: `/news`, `/models` and `/quests` put the GitHub button at the bottom of the sidebar, while `/sign-in` had its own shell with an in-page banner and nothing in the sidebar. On phones the drawer starts closed, so `/news` showed no sign-in at all, and the `/sign-in` drawer had an empty bottom.

- Moves `/sign-in` under the `_dashboard` layout (URL unchanged), so it gets the same sidebar/drawer sign-in button; it keeps the auto-opening dialog and the signed-in redirect
- Shows the "Create your Pollinations account" banner on every signed-out page below `lg`, where the drawer is closed; desktop drops it since the sidebar button is always visible
- Insets the banner 16px on phones and tightens the wrapped gap between the sentence and button
- Removes the unused `defaultOpen`/`message` props and folds the one-use sign-in trigger into the banner, which shares its dialog with `/sign-in`

gist.headline: Sign-in finds the front door
gist.blurb: The sign-in button stops hiding in a closed mobile drawer. Signed-out pages get a phone-friendly banner, while the dashboard keeps one shared sign-in path.
gist.summary: Moves /sign-in into the dashboard layout and adds a signed-out account banner below the lg breakpoint, making sign-in visible on mobile /news, /models, and /quests pages while preserving the dialog and signed-in redirect.
gist.impact: On phones, signed-out visitors get a visible GitHub sign-in button without opening the drawer; on desktop, the sidebar button remains the sign-in entry point.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy dashboard garden with a small phone showing a visible account banner and a desktop monitor showing its sidebar sign-in button. Polli, wearing a tiny guide's scarf, points the monitor robot toward the easy-to-find mobile button; flowers and code-plants connect the two screens.
